problem: Given that $x=-\frac{1}{4}$ is a solution to the equation $36{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}+4x+1=0,$ find the remaining solutions.
worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=36{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}+4x+1.$ Since $x=-\frac{1}{4}$ is a root of $f(x),$ then according to the factor theorem $(x+\frac{1}{4})$ is a factor of $f(x).$ 

We find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+\frac{1}{4})$ using synthetic division.

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{4}$ | $36$ | $9$ | $4$ | $1$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-9$ | $0$ | $-1$ |
|  | $36$ | $0$ | $4$ | $0$ |

Thus, $f(x)=(x+\frac{1}{4})(36{x}^{2}+4).$ 

To find the remaining two roots, we solve $36{x}^{2}+4=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}36{x}^{2}+4 & =0 \\ 36{x}^{2} & =-4 \\ {x}^{2} & =-\frac{1}{9} \\ {x}^{2} & ={(\frac{1}{3}\text{i})}^{2} \\ x & =\pm \frac{1}{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to our original equation are $x=-\frac{1}{4},\,\pm \frac{1}{3}\text{i}.$
